metadata.description: Consolidated toy-scale measurement of Wesolowski Algorithm 3 concrete cost
metadata.counting_method: Analytical F_{p^2}-multiplication count per step. For each neighbor-finding call (find roots of Phi_ell(j_known, X) in F_{p^2}): (1) Compute j^2,...,j^{ell+1}: ell mults. (2) Root-finding via repeated squaring in F_{p^2}[x]/(f(x)): 2*log2(p) * ((ell+1)^2 + (ell+1)) mults for x^{p^2} computation, plus (ell+1)^2 for GCD, plus (ell+1)*2*log2(p) for factor splitting. Frobenius j->j^p is conjugation in F_{p^2}=F_p[T]/(T^2-s), counted as free. Collision lookup costs 2 mults per check (hash computation).
limitations: Operation count is analytical (based on schoolbook polynomial arithmetic), not instrumented at gate level
Does not account for potential subquadratic polynomial multiplication (Karatsuba/FFT)
Frobenius counted as free (correct for F_{p^2} = F_p[T]/(T^2-s))
Walk cost uses same 2-isogeny stepping as table construction
P0 at toy scale is much higher than theory predicts (table covers large fraction of SS graph)

extrapolation_analysis.method: Linear fit of ops/entry vs log2(p^2) from measured data, combined with paper parameters

paper_parameters_nist_i.assumption: 1 F_{p^2}-operation per table entry (stated as deliberate lower bound in paper)

measured_ops_per_entry_scaling.dominant_cost_component: Root finding in F_{p^2}[x]/(f) via repeated squaring: O(ell^2 * log(p^2))

uncertainty_sources: Schoolbook arithmetic assumed (Karatsuba/FFT would reduce ops/entry)
P0 from paper uses single-path lower bound (Remark 1 says actual P0 is higher)
At crypto scale, multiple-path bonus likely negligible (table is ~2^92 entries vs ~2^85 total SS curves)
Modular polynomial evaluation cost varies with ℓ distribution in the tree
Batched evaluation (Robert suggestion in paper) could reduce cost

P0_bonus_analysis.description: Empirical P0 exceeds theoretical lower bound by large factor at toy scale
P0_bonus_analysis.interpretation: Multiple B-smooth isogenies E->E^{(p)} exist (Remark 1 in paper). At toy scale, the table covers a significant fraction of the SS graph, making collisions very likely. At crypto scale (~2^92 entries in a graph of ~2^85*p/12 curves... wait, SS graph has ~p/12 nodes), the table still covers a measurable fraction, but the smoothness condition becomes the actual bottleneck. The P0 bonus likely persists but at a different magnitude.
P0_bonus_analysis.crypto_scale_expectation: Conservative: assume P0 = u^{-u} (paper lower bound). May overestimate cost.

comparison_to_team_hypothesis.status: CONSISTENT - measured ops/entry correction of 2^12 above 1-op-per-entry lower bound
